macro.topic: Turkey: money-market fund (PPF) scandal — liquidations, asset freezes, and the debate over state guarantees

views.view: Shared that the Ministry of Justice froze the assets of 46 legal entities, 18 funds, and 42 individuals after examining the largest cash outflows from funds between July 1 and September 16. As his own view, argued that Takasbank is also responsible for the weak quality of collateral, that citizens will not pay for the negligence, and that everyone with money in PPFs will get it back. Shared economist Ozgur Demirtas's analysis describing how fund companies inflated illiquid stocks and presented them as collateral, and welcomed Treasury and Finance Minister Mehmet Simsek's statement that no action would be taken against innocent investors and companies.
views.quote: Takasbank is responsible too, you all saw that shoddy collateral. Citizens will not pay for this negligence; everyone with money in #PPF will get it, people have become beggars for their own LIQUID money, this will not be forgotten.

macro.topic: China is considering easing export restrictions on Nvidia's RTX Pro 5500 chips

views.view: Reported, citing The Information, that Beijing may allow companies like Alibaba and ByteDance to buy Nvidia's new RTX Pro 5500 chips; ByteDance alone is weighing an order of about 1 million chips, shipments could start in late December with roughly 500,000 chips targeted per quarter for China, priced at about $13,000 per chip, with approval timing and conditions still unclear.
views.quote: CHINA WEIGHS EASING RESTRICTIONS ON NEW $NVDA CHIP PURCHASES... ByteDance alone is weighing an order for about 1M chips.

views.view: Believes that if the news is confirmed, Nvidia's revenue estimates could be revised upward and the stock could be re-rated.
views.quote: If approval comes through, this could mean upward revisions to Nvidia's revenue estimates and a re-rating of the stock. Buckle up.

views.view: Shared the news with a cautious tone, emphasizing that approval is not yet finalized and that Reuters could not independently confirm the report.
views.quote: Reuters could not independently confirm the report; there is no finalized approval yet.

macro.topic: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang: total investment commitment across the AI ecosystem could exceed $100 billion

views.view: Reported that Nvidia's all-in investment across the AI ecosystem could reach $100 billion, larger than the CHIPS Act's total $52.7B in semiconductor funding; listed concrete commitments such as up to $100B for OpenAI, up to $10B for Anthropic, $5B for Intel, up to $2.1B investment rights for IREN, and $2B for CoreWeave.
views.quote: All in, we might be like a hundred billion dollars.

macro.topic: In the debate over the US bond market and debt burden, the view that AI/robotics growth will dominate

views.view: Wrote that the yen carry trade crowd has been predicting a bond market collapse for years but has missed a huge rally in the process; that US debt is the biggest problem, with both parties agreeing only on more spending, but that he believes AI and robotics infrastructure investment tailwinds will dwarf these headwinds into the 2030s.
views.quote: US debt I think is biggest issue of all (with nobody even seeming interested in tackling it, more spending is only thing both sides of gov agree on?) but despite it all I believe the AI / robotics buildout tailwinds will dwarf the headwinds into 2030s.

macro.topic: Debate over a US diesel export ban

views.view: Reported that Goldman Sachs estimates each week of a diesel export ban would cut US retail diesel prices by about 25 cents a gallon from the current $6.50, but warned a longer ban would push gasoline prices higher once storage fills, while Energy Secretary Wright said last week that such a ban wouldn't work.
views.quote: Goldman Sachs estimates each week of a diesel export ban would cut US retail diesel prices by about 25 cents a gallon from the current $6.50, but warned a longer ban would push gasoline prices higher once storage fills. Energy Sec. Wright said last week a ban wouldn't work.
